items.question: Work Summary
items.problem: Expected "Most of my work has been building data and ML infrastructure rather than one-off analyses. At Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus I own major parts of the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection system: the repository and CI scaffold, the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, and the public detection API. The modeling side is temporal sequence modeling over event streams with RNN and Transformer-style approaches, anomaly scoring, and a learning-to-rank layer that prioritizes alerts, because a detector that fires constantly just creates a second problem for the analysts reading it. I also built an LLM explanation layer over retrieval so outputs are interpretable to a human. Before that, at Intelehealth, I built a resource-availability scoring pipeline in Python across 32 villages and designed an evaluation framework comparing AI-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard using stratified sampling. That work is where I got interested in reliability and correctness as engineering problems, not afterthoughts. I study Applied Mathematics and Statistics and Economics at Johns Hopkins, and a data platform supporting electronic markets is exactly the kind of system where throughput, correctness, and state consistency all have to hold at once."; page shows "(empty)"
